source.title: Statistical Characteristics of Deep Representations: An Empirical Investigation
source.authors: Daeyoung Choi; Kyungeun Lee; Duhun Hwang; Wonjong Rhee

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper and supplementary materials; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports dropout comparisons with a baseline and finds mixed performance effects across datasets and settings, qualifying the claim that dropout lowers test error in some regimes.
record.gate_note: The study compares test performance for dropout and baseline models. Its representation statistics and their relation to performance do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or the training–test gap.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares dropout with an unregularized baseline on held-out classification performance using a different experimental recipe. MNIST results establish benefits and failures; contradictory or missing metric labels prevent secure interpretation of the CIFAR comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: trying and tuning representation regularizers can improve performance, but the authors find no consistent relationship between the measured representation statistics and performance. Effects through learning dynamics are proposed as a possibility, not demonstrated causally.
record.recipe_differences: Compares representation regularizers and dropout against baselines; it does not reproduce the original dropout study's stated method. It tunes regularizer loss weights using validation performance.
record.method_sensitivity: Dropout comparisons vary with dataset, data size, layer width, optimizer, and number of classes. The paper also reports that regularizer behavior and performance vary with the layer to which regularization is applied.

fits_no_version.finding: Manipulating representation correlation, sparsity and rank produces no consistent relationship with held-out performance; the correlation and sparsity plots use single runs selected for performance comparable to baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation statistics do not consistently predict held-out performance across the tested regularizers and settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout produces strongly correlated activations in the representation visualizations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout need not produce decorrelated hidden representations.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Neural Networks
record.problems: The correlation and sparsity versus performance plots use one training and test run per model and include only results comparable to baseline. Several cited supplementary table values are test accuracies or errors rather than training–test gaps; this study does not measure generalization gap directly.
record.rows_left_out: No dropout comparisons in the main Table 3; extracted the separately reported dropout-versus-baseline values from Supplementary Tables 6–8. Other regularizer outcomes are outside the dropout claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting compared with natural-label training and held-out performance.
Width increases beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold; training error and convergence are not established.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons on the same image task and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under the stated tuning protocol. The optimizer conditions use fixed, different learning rates without establishing comparable tuning.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.

A dropout-rate sweep establishing excessive-dropout underfitting; the original very-small-set boundary; removal of dropout and weight decay together with augmentation. Reduced-data conditions are tested, including 1,000 examples.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations, training–test gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Influence-based identification and removal of memorized training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V6. CIFAR values are transcribed correctly, but their interpretation requires metric clarification: Table 7 explicitly says error despite accuracy-like trends, while Table 8 supplies no metric label. Do not publish directional CIFAR verdicts by silently assuming either interpretation. Standard deviations alone do not establish significance.

versions.untested_parts: Widening beyond interpolation and test error.
Large versus small batch effects on the generalization gap.

The paper tests dropout performance in several settings, but does not report the stated very-small-training-set and excessive-dropout-dose comparisons as such; it does not test removing dropout and weight decay together with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
